newsitem.title: GERMANY: French-led group buys Germany's Spar retail chain.
newsitem.headline: French-led group buys Germany's Spar retail chain.

text.p: A controlling stake in German supermarket chain Spar Handels AG has been bought by a group led by France's Intermarche, sellers' group NHH Norddeutsche Handels Holding GmbH said on Wednesday.
The Swiss-based buyers' group, which is 51 percent held by Intermarche unit ITM Entreprises SA, is buying a stake of 75 percent plus one share in Spar, Germany's fourth largest food retailer.
The remaining 49 percent of the buyers' group is held by investors Friedrich Dieckell, Berhard Schmidt, Klaus-Peter Schneidewind and WCM Beteiligungs- und Grundbesitz AG.
Spar, with nearly 4,000 stores, aims to boost annual sales to 25 billion marks by the end of the decade from the current 21.6 billion marks.
ITM, with 2,200 stores, has sales of about 40 billion marks.
